profile_fields.state: State or UT the farmer lives in
profile_fields.owns_land: true if the farmland is recorded in the farmer's own name
profile_fields.land_hectares: Size of the farmer's land in hectares (1 acre = 0.4047 hectare)
profile_fields.pays_income_tax: true if the farmer or anyone in the family paid income tax in the last assessment year
profile_fields.govt_employee_or_pensioner: true if the farmer or a family member has a government job or draws a government pension of Rs 10,000 or more a month

schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.benefit: Rs 6,000 a year, paid as three instalments of Rs 2,000 straight into the bank account of every landholding farmer family.

eligibility.notes: Land must be in the family's name in state land records; tenant farmers and sharecroppers are not covered. Also excluded: institutional landholders, present or former holders of constitutional posts, ministers, MPs, MLAs, mayors, zila panchayat chairpersons, practising professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, architects) and NRIs. Class IV / Group D / MTS government staff ARE allowed. Pensioners are excluded only if the pension is Rs 10,000 or more a month. eKYC is compulsory.

documents: Aadhaar card
Land record in your name (khatauni / khasra / record of rights / patta)
Bank passbook of an account linked to Aadhaar
Mobile number (for OTP and status messages)
online_steps: Open pmkisan.gov.in and click 'New Farmer Registration' in the Farmers Corner
Enter Aadhaar number, mobile number and state, and verify with the OTP (only on the official site)
Fill in personal details, land details (survey / khata number) and bank details; upload the land record
Submit and save the registration number
Complete eKYC: OTP eKYC on the portal, face eKYC on the PM-Kisan mobile app, or biometric eKYC at a CSC
Check approval under 'Know Your Status' on the portal
offline_places: Block or district agriculture office (state nodal officer)

schemes.name: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana) — crop insurance
schemes.benefit: Insurance money if your notified crop is damaged by drought, flood, hailstorm, pests, disease or other natural causes. You pay only a small premium: at most 2% of the sum insured for kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for rabi, 5% for annual commercial or horticultural crops. The government pays the rest.

eligibility.notes: Open to ALL farmers, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers, who grow a crop notified for their area in that season. Farmers with a crop loan / KCC are covered automatically unless they opt out in writing; others enrol voluntarily. Enrolment closes before the state's cut-off date (commonly 31 July for kharif and 31 December for rabi; check locally). Notified crops and areas are decided by the state.

documents: Aadhaar card
Bank passbook
Land record (khasra / record of rights), or for tenant farmers and sharecroppers the tenancy or crop-sharing agreement / declaration your state asks for
Sowing certificate or self-declaration of the crop you have sown
Mobile number
online_steps: Open pmfby.gov.in and click 'Farmer Corner' > 'Farmer Application' (or use the 'Crop Insurance' mobile app)
Register with your mobile number and log in with the OTP (only on the official site or app)
Choose state, district, season and crop; enter land details and upload the documents
Pay your share of the premium online
Save the application / policy number and track it under 'Application Status'
If the crop is damaged, report it within 72 hours on the app, on 14447, or to your bank or insurance company
offline_places: Your bank branch (farmers with a KCC or crop loan are usually enrolled by the bank; confirm there)
Office of the insurance company appointed for your district

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
schemes.benefit: A low-interest farm loan card for seeds, fertiliser, labour and other crop costs, and also for dairy, poultry and fisheries. Interest is 7% a year, and only 4% if you repay on time, on crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh (being raised to Rs 5 lakh as announced in Budget 2025; ask your bank). No collateral is needed for a limit up to Rs 2 lakh.

eligibility.notes: For owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, self-help groups and joint liability groups of farmers, and dairy, poultry and fisheries farmers. Farmers above 60 need a co-borrower (usually a legal heir). The bank takes the final decision on the loan limit.

documents: Filled KCC application form (from the bank, or the one-page form on pmkisan.gov.in)
Two passport-size photographs
Identity proof (Aadhaar, voter ID, PAN or driving licence)
Address proof (Aadhaar, voter ID, ration card)
Land record certified by the revenue office; tenant farmers and sharecroppers give proof of cultivation / tenancy as the bank asks
List of crops grown with area (cropping pattern)
Security papers only if the limit is above Rs 2 lakh
online_steps: Open your bank's website or app and search 'Kisan Credit Card' (for example SBI YONO Krishi); fill the online form
PM-KISAN beneficiaries can download the one-page KCC form from pmkisan.gov.in (Farmers Corner > Download KCC Form) and submit it to the bank that pays their PM-KISAN money
Visit the branch once with the original documents for verification
The bank issues the KCC (a RuPay debit card) and fixes the loan limit for 5 years
offline_places: Any bank branch: public sector, private, regional rural bank or cooperative bank, best where you already have an account
Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) in your village
Nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or a KCC camp (Ghar Ghar KCC Abhiyan)
schemes.official_website: https://pmkisan.gov.in (KCC form under Farmers Corner); your bank's website for the online form
schemes.helpline: Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551 (toll-free); your bank's customer care

schemes.name: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — farmer pension
schemes.benefit: A guaranteed pension of Rs 3,000 every month after age 60 for small and marginal farmers. You pay a small amount every month until 60 (Rs 55 to Rs 200, depending on your age when you join) and the central government pays the same amount into your account.

eligibility.notes: Small and marginal farmers with cultivable land up to 2 hectares in their name as per state land records, aged 18 to 40 when joining. Not for farmers already covered by NPS, EPFO, ESIC, PM-SYM or NPS-Traders, or those in the PM-KISAN exclusion list (income-tax payers, government employees, higher-pension holders, professionals). PM-KISAN beneficiaries can pay the contribution from their PM-KISAN money. Spouse gets 50% family pension after the farmer's death.

documents: Aadhaar card
Savings bank passbook or Jan Dhan account (or your PM-KISAN account)
Land record showing up to 2 hectares (khasra / khatauni)
Mobile number
Age proof (Aadhaar is usually enough)
online_steps: Open maandhan.in and click 'Self Enrollment'
Enter your mobile number and verify with the OTP (only on the official site)
Fill in personal, bank and land details and choose auto-debit for the monthly contribution
Pay the first contribution and download your Kisan Pension Card; note the KPAN number
Contributions are auto-debited every month until age 60; pension starts at 60
offline_places: Nearest Common Service Centre (CSC): enrolment is free, the operator registers you
Block or district agriculture office (state nodal officer)

schemes.name: Soil Health Card (SHC)
schemes.benefit: Free testing of your field's soil and a card that shows its nutrient status (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, organic carbon, micronutrients) with the right fertiliser dose for your crops. Saves fertiliser money and improves yield.

eligibility.notes: Every farmer can get one; there are no exclusions and no fee. One card per plot. Soil samples are collected in cycles by the state agriculture department, so timing depends on your state.

documents: Aadhaar or any identity card
Land details: village, survey / khasra number
Mobile number
online_steps: Open soilhealth.dac.gov.in or install the 'Soil Health Card' mobile app
Register as a farmer with your mobile number and verify with the OTP (only on the official site or app)
Request soil testing for your plot, or check the status of a sample already collected
Once the lab uploads the result, download or print your Soil Health Card with your sample number
offline_places: Village agriculture extension officer / krishi sahayak
Block agriculture office or the state soil testing laboratory
